account: Something more than an ordinary lighting inspection seems to be planned for eighteen o'clock in the great hall. My written appointment calls it a lighting inspection, but I personally heard builder ask neighbour to escort me there for a 'service acknowledgement.' Neighbour agreed and will host our usual fifteen o'clock tea first. Builder subsequently described the lighting as on track and said innkeeper coordinates hospitality. Neighbour has been soliciting voluntary bread and grain contributions for a community supper, though she told me its time and venue were not confirmed and did not name its organisers. Just now several townsfolk reported seeing innkeeper carrying a sack of bread at market. That fits preparations for hospitality, although I have not seen that bread myself. Builder, neighbour and innkeeper therefore seem involved in some coordinated gathering, perhaps a surprise acknowledgement of my service accompanied by a supper. I do not yet know that for certain, nor whether the supper and acknowledgement are the same event. Baker and freight may be involved in supplies; reports have linked them to discussions at the bakery, but the repeated claim about a bridge or port change is unsubstantiated, and neighbour explicitly denied knowing of any such proposal. Today I attended the mill for the grain inspection, went home at noon, and have returned for thirteen o'clock council letters. My request for correspondence apparently did not reach secretary, so I still need to speak to them directly. I should keep my remaining appointments while finding out what is actually arranged rather than treating market rumours as facts.
